pl900: Which Power Platform product do you use to build low-code business apps?
Power Apps is the low-code tool for building business apps.
Which type of Power Apps app is built from the data model in Dataverse and gets its layout generated automatically?
Model-driven apps are built from Dataverse tables, forms and views; the layout is generated for you.
Which type of Power Apps app gives you full control over the layout, like designing on a blank canvas?
Canvas apps let you place every control exactly where you want it.
Where do Power Apps and Power Automate store business data by default in the Power Platform?
Microsoft Dataverse is the built-in data platform of the Power Platform.
Which type of Power Automate flow runs on a fixed schedule?
Scheduled cloud flows run at a time and frequency you set.
Which type of Power Automate flow is started manually, for example with a button?
Instant cloud flows are triggered manually, for example from a button in Power Automate, Teams or Power Apps.
A flow should start automatically when a new email arrives in Outlook. Which flow type do you use?
Automated cloud flows are triggered by an event, such as a new email.
You need to automate an old Windows application that has no API. What do you use?
Desktop flows use robotic process automation (RPA) to work with the user interface of desktop apps.
Which Power Automate action processes every item in a list?
Apply to each loops through every item in an array or list.
Every Power Automate flow starts with which element?
A trigger is the event that starts the flow; actions follow it.
Which Power Automate expression returns the current date and time in UTC?
utcNow() returns the current date and time in UTC.
Which Power Automate action sends a request and pauses the flow until someone approves or rejects it?
Start and wait for an approval
Post message in a chat or channel
Start and wait for an approval sends the approval and waits for the response.
Where do you look first to troubleshoot why a cloud flow failed?
The run history shows each run and the action that failed, with inputs and outputs.
What is the difference between attended and unattended desktop flows?
Unattended flows run without a user signed in on the machine
Unattended flows need a person to click Start each time
Attended flows run only in the cloud
Attended flows cannot use UI automation
Unattended RPA runs on a machine without a signed-in user; attended runs while a user is working on the machine.
Which Power Automate capability analyzes how a business process runs to find bottlenecks?
Process mining analyzes event data to show how processes really run and where they slow down.
What can Copilot in Power Automate do?
Create a flow from a description in natural language
You can describe the flow you need and Copilot builds a first version.
What is a connector in the Power Platform?
A wrapper around an API that lets apps and flows talk to a service
A type of Power BI visual
Connectors wrap an API so Power Apps, Power Automate and Copilot Studio can use a service.
Which of these connectors is a premium connector?
SQL Server is premium; SharePoint, Outlook and OneDrive for Business are standard connectors.
You need to connect to your company's own REST API that has no existing connector. What do you create?
A custom connector describes your own API so it can be used like any other connector.
What do data loss prevention (DLP) policies control?
The size of a Dataverse database
How long data stays in Dataverse
Which users can open Power BI
Which connectors can be used together in apps and flows
DLP policies group connectors (for example Business and Non-business) so data cannot flow between the wrong services.
Where do administrators manage environments and DLP policies?
The Power Platform admin center is used to manage environments, policies and capacity.
What is an environment in the Power Platform?
A container for apps, flows, data and other resources
Environments separate resources, for example development, test and production.
Which environment type is meant for one maker to build and test, free of charge?
Developer environments are personal environments for building and testing.
Which statement about the default environment is true?
Every tenant has one and all licensed users can create apps there
It must be created by an admin
Each tenant has one default environment; by default all users in the tenant can make apps and flows there.
Extra governance and admin features for an environment
Managed Environments add governance features such as sharing limits, usage insights and solution checker enforcement.
Which tool kit helps organizations govern and monitor Power Platform adoption?
The CoE Starter Kit collects inventory and usage data and helps with governance.
Which Dataverse table type is used for items like emails, tasks and appointments?
Activity tables represent actions that can be scheduled or tracked, such as emails and tasks.
Which Dataverse column type creates a link to a record in another table?
A lookup column creates a many-to-one relationship to another table.
Which Dataverse column type gives users a fixed list of values to choose from?
A choice column holds a predefined set of options.
Which Dataverse column type aggregates values from related records, for example total of open opportunities?
Rollup columns calculate aggregates (sum, count, min, max) over related records.
What can you do with a Dataverse business rule without writing code?
Make a column required or set a value based on a condition
Business rules apply simple logic such as show/hide, required, set value and validation.
What does a Dataverse security role define?
Privileges and access levels for tables
The color theme of an app
Security roles define what a user can create, read, write, delete etc. and at what level.
Which feature restricts access to individual sensitive columns, such as salary, in Dataverse?
Column security profiles control who can read or update specific columns.
Which Dataverse feature records who changed a record and when?
Auditing logs changes to records and columns.
What is a solution in the Power Platform used for?
Packaging apps, flows and tables to move them between environments
Solutions package components for application lifecycle management (ALM).
Which type of solution should you deploy to a production environment?
Managed solutions are used for deployment; unmanaged solutions are used in development.
Which components are part of a model-driven app? (Choose two.)
Model-driven apps use forms, views, charts and dashboards; screens and galleries belong to canvas apps.
Which canvas app control shows a list of records?
A gallery displays a repeating set of records.
Which Power Fx function submits the changes in an Edit form control?
SubmitForm saves the changes made in a form control to the data source.
Which Power Fx function moves the user to another screen?
Navigate opens a different screen, optionally with a transition.
Which Power Fx function creates or updates a record directly in a data source?
Patch creates or modifies records without a form.
Power Fx, the formula language in canvas apps, is based on which product?
Power Fx is based on Excel formulas.
What happens when a canvas app formula is not delegable?
Only the first part of the data (500 records by default) is processed locally
Non-delegable queries work only on the first rows, 500 by default (can be raised to 2000).
What is a component library in Power Apps used for?
Reusing components across many canvas apps
Component libraries hold reusable components that many apps can use.
Which feature lets makers create a canvas app by describing it in plain language?
Copilot in Power Apps can generate tables and an app from a description.
A built-in, low-code data platform for building apps inside Microsoft Teams
Dataverse for Teams provides tables and apps directly in Teams.
How can users run Power Apps on their phone?
With the Power Apps mobile app
The Power Apps mobile app runs canvas and model-driven apps on iOS and Android.
What guides users through defined stages, such as Qualify → Develop → Close, in a model-driven app?
Business process flows show stages and steps at the top of a form.
Dynamics 365 Sales and Customer Service store their data in:
Customer engagement apps of Dynamics 365 are built on Dataverse.
Which Power Platform product is used to build external-facing business websites?
Power Pages is for secure, low-code websites for external users.
What do table permissions control in Power Pages?
Which Dataverse data site visitors can read or change
Table permissions control access of site users to Dataverse records.
Where does Power Pages store its data?
Power Pages sites use Dataverse as their data store.
Which product do you use to build AI agents (chatbots) with little or no code?
Copilot Studio (formerly Power Virtual Agents) is used to build agents.
In Copilot Studio, what starts a topic?
Trigger phrases or a description that matches what the user says
Topics are triggered by phrases or by intent recognition from the description.
Which Copilot Studio feature answers questions using knowledge sources such as websites and documents?
Generative answers use the knowledge sources you add to answer questions.
How can a Copilot Studio agent perform an action such as creating a record in another system?
Call a Power Automate flow or connector action
Agents can call flows, connectors and other actions.
Where can a Copilot Studio agent be published? (Choose two.)
Agents can be published to channels such as Teams and websites.
What do entities do in Copilot Studio?
Recognize information such as dates, numbers or cities in the user's message
Entities extract structured information from what the user says.
What can an agent do when it cannot help the user?
Escalate (hand off) to a human agent
The Escalate system topic can hand the conversation to a live agent.
Which Power Platform feature provides prebuilt and custom AI models for Power Apps and Power Automate?
AI Builder adds AI models such as document processing and prediction.
Which AI Builder model extracts fields like vendor name and total from invoices?
The invoice processing model reads key fields from invoices.
Which AI Builder model tells you if a text is positive, negative or neutral?
Sentiment analysis detects positive, negative or neutral text.
Which AI Builder model predicts a yes/no outcome from historical Dataverse data?
Prediction models learn from historical data to predict outcomes.
Which AI Builder model finds and counts items in an image?
Object detection recognizes and counts objects in images.
Which identity service do users sign in with to use the Power Platform?
The Power Platform uses Microsoft Entra ID (formerly Azure AD).
Which Power Apps license lets a user run unlimited apps?
Power Apps Premium is the per-user plan for unlimited apps.
Which Power BI tool do you use to build reports on a Windows computer?
Power BI Desktop is the free authoring tool for reports and data models.
In which Power BI component do you connect to and transform data?
Power Query is used to get and shape data.
Which language do you use to create measures and calculated columns in Power BI?
DAX (Data Analysis Expressions) is used for calculations in the model.
In Power Query, where can you see and undo each transformation?
Every transformation is listed in Applied steps.
What is the file extension of a Power BI Desktop file?
Power BI Desktop files use the .pbix extension.
In the Power BI service, what is a dashboard?
A single page with tiles that can come from several reports
Dashboards are single-page canvases of pinned tiles from one or more reports.
Where is Power BI content created and shared by a team?
Workspaces hold reports, dashboards and semantic models for collaboration.
What is a Power BI app?
A packaged set of reports and dashboards distributed to many users
Power BI apps bundle content from a workspace for consumers.
Which Power BI feature lets users ask questions about data in natural language?
The Q&A visual answers questions written in plain language.
Which feature restricts the rows a user can see in a Power BI report?
RLS filters data per user or role.
What does the on-premises data gateway do?
Connects cloud services to data stored on-premises
The gateway securely connects Power BI, Power Apps and Power Automate to on-premises data.
What is the difference between Import and DirectQuery in Power BI?
DirectQuery copies all data into the .pbix
DirectQuery queries the source at report time; Import copies data into the model
Import stores a copy that is refreshed; DirectQuery sends queries to the source each time.
How do you keep imported data in a published Power BI semantic model up to date?
Scheduled refresh reloads imported data from the source.
Which visual is best for showing a trend over time?
Line charts show how values change over time.
Which Power BI visual shows a single important number, such as total sales?
A card shows one value clearly.
In a star schema, which tables hold numeric events like sales amounts?
Fact tables store measurable events; dimension tables describe them.
What is the most common relationship cardinality between a dimension table and a fact table?
One dimension row relates to many fact rows.
At which levels can you apply filters in the Power BI filters pane? (Choose two.)
Filters can be applied to a visual, a page or the whole report.
Which report type is best for pixel-perfect, printable documents such as invoices?
Paginated reports are designed for printing and exact layouts.
Users usually need which license to share and collaborate on Power BI content in the service?
Power BI Pro (or content in a Premium/Fabric capacity)
Sharing generally requires Power BI Pro, unless the content is in a capacity that allows free users to view it.
Which Power BI visual lets users start a Power Automate flow from a report?
The Power Automate visual runs a flow with data from the report.
Where can you view Power BI reports on a phone?
The Power BI mobile app shows reports and dashboards on iOS and Android.
Which Power BI feature lets you go from a summary page to a detail page for a selected item?
Drillthrough opens a target page filtered on the selected value.
Which statement about Power Apps and Microsoft Teams is true?
Teams cannot show any Power Apps
Apps in Teams cannot use data
Canvas apps can be added as tabs in Teams
Only Power BI works in Teams
Apps can be embedded in Teams as tabs or built directly in Teams.
A SharePoint list item is created and you want to notify a manager. Which trigger fits?
When a HTTP request is received
The SharePoint trigger starts the flow when a new item is created.
Which control in a canvas app lets users pick a value from a list?
Drop-down and combo box controls show a list of values.
Which Power Automate action lets the flow take different paths based on a yes/no check?
Condition creates If yes / If no branches.
Which Power Automate action waits for a period of time before continuing?
Delay pauses the flow for a set amount of time.
Where can makers start quickly from prebuilt flows for common scenarios?
Templates provide ready-made flows you can customize.
Which statement about standard and premium connectors is true?
Standard connectors need Power BI Pro
Premium connectors only work in Power BI
Premium connectors need a premium license
All connectors are free for everyone
Premium connectors require a Power Apps or Power Automate premium license.
Which Dataverse feature helps prevent creating the same customer twice?
Duplicate detection rules find possible duplicates when records are created or imported.
What organizes users in Dataverse to control which records they can see by structure, for example by region?
Business units define the security hierarchy for records and roles.
Which type of Dataverse relationship does a lookup column create?
A lookup creates a one-to-many relationship.
You want views, forms and charts based on Dataverse tables with little design work. What should you build?
Model-driven apps give you these components out of the box.
mb310: What is a main account in Dynamics 365 Finance?
A bank account in Cash and bank management
An account in the chart of accounts, such as 110110 Bank
Main accounts are the accounts of the chart of accounts; together with financial dimensions they form ledger accounts.
What are financial dimensions used for?
To analyze and report transactions, for example by department or cost center
Financial dimensions add analysis values to transactions.
Which statement about the chart of accounts is true?
A chart of accounts can contain only 10 accounts
The chart of accounts is set up per user
One chart of accounts can be shared by several legal entities
Each legal entity must have its own chart of accounts
A chart of accounts is shared data and can be assigned to many ledgers.
What does an account structure define?
Which financial dimensions and values are valid together with main accounts
Account structures control valid combinations of main accounts and dimensions.
What do advanced rules do in Finance?
Add extra financial dimensions to an account structure when criteria are met
Advanced rule structures add dimensions only for certain main accounts or values.
On which page do you assign the chart of accounts, fiscal calendar and accounting currency to a legal entity?
The Ledger page holds the chart of accounts, account structures, fiscal calendar and currencies.
Which ledger period status temporarily stops posting but lets you reopen the period later?
On hold blocks posting; it can be set back to Open. Permanently closed cannot be reopened.
In the ledger calendar, how can you allow only some modules to post in a period?
Set module access levels for the period
Module access lets you restrict posting per module, for example only General ledger.
What does a posting profile define?
Which ledger accounts subledger transactions (e.g. customer or vendor) post to
Posting profiles map subledger transactions to ledger accounts.
In a vendor posting profile, the summary account represents:
The summary account is the AP control account.
The journal type, voucher number sequence and optional approval
Journal names control voucher series, journal type and approval settings.
Which journal do you use to post a manual adjustment directly to the general ledger?
The general journal is used for ledger postings such as adjustments.
You post the same rent entry every month. What helps you do this?
Periodic journals store entries that you retrieve and post on a schedule.
What do ledger allocation rules do?
Distribute an amount across several accounts or dimension values
Allocation rules split amounts, for example shared costs across departments.
Which feature spreads a prepaid expense over several periods?
Accrual schemes post an amount over a number of periods.
How do you post an entry that reverses automatically in the next period?
Enter a reversing date on the journal line
A reversing entry with a reversing date creates the reversal automatically.
Which workspace helps manage month-end and year-end closing tasks?
Financial period close lets you create closing schedules, tasks and owners.
What happens to profit and loss balances during the year-end close?
They move to the bank account
They are copied to the budget
They are transferred to the retained earnings account
Year-end close transfers P&L results to retained earnings and creates opening balances.
A main account of type Expense will, at year end:
Keep its balance as an opening balance
Expense and revenue (profit and loss) accounts are closed to retained earnings.
Which main account type carries its balance forward as an opening balance into the new year?
Balance sheet accounts (asset, liability, equity) carry forward.
Combining financial results of several legal entities
Consolidation combines the results of subsidiaries into a consolidated company or report.
What accounts do you set up for intercompany accounting between two legal entities?
Due to and due from accounts
Intercompany accounting uses due to/due from accounts in each entity.
Which process recalculates foreign currency balances of ledger accounts at the current exchange rate?
Foreign currency revaluation adjusts balances for exchange rate changes.
What is the purpose of exchange rate types?
To keep different sets of rates, for example for daily use and for budgeting
Exchange rate types let you maintain different rate sets.
Why would you set a reporting currency on the ledger?
To record transactions also in a second currency, for example the group currency
The reporting currency stores amounts in an additional currency for reporting.
How is sales tax determined on a transaction line?
From the intersection of the sales tax group and the item sales tax group
Sales tax codes that exist in both groups apply to the line.
What does a sales tax settlement period define?
The tax authority and the period interval for settling and reporting tax
Settlement periods group tax codes by authority and reporting intervals.
Which feature matches bank statement lines with posted bank transactions?
Advanced bank reconciliation imports statements and matches them to transactions.
A file of issued checks sent to the bank to help prevent check fraud
Positive pay files let the bank verify checks before paying them.
Which module do you use to set up company bank accounts?
Bank accounts are set up in Cash and bank management.
What is three-way matching in accounts payable?
Comparing the purchase order, product receipt and vendor invoice
Three-way matching checks price and quantity across PO, receipt and invoice.
The purchase order and the vendor invoice
The product receipt and the bank statement
Two-way matching compares invoice and purchase order prices.
What does a price tolerance percentage do in invoice matching?
Allows a small price difference before a matching discrepancy is shown
Differences within the tolerance do not block the invoice.
Which feature suggests vendor invoices to pay based on due date or cash discount?
A payment proposal finds invoices to pay in the vendor payment journal.
What does a method of payment define?
The due date of an invoice
How a payment is made and which account it posts to, e.g. a bank account
Methods of payment define payment type, account and file formats.
What do terms of payment calculate?
The due date of an invoice
Terms of payment, such as Net 30, calculate the due date.
A discount if the customer or vendor pays before a certain date
A discount for buying more items
Cash discounts reward early payment, e.g. 2% if paid within 10 days.
How do you stop a vendor from receiving any new invoices or payments?
Put the vendor on hold (for example All)
The On hold setting blocks selected transaction types for the vendor.
What is the invoice register used for?
Recording vendor invoices before they are approved and distributed
The invoice register records invoices to a temporary account until approval.
A payment after the due date
A payment made before the vendor's invoice is received
Prepayments are payments made in advance, later applied to the invoice.
What does vendor invoice automation do?
Imports invoices and can match and submit them to workflow automatically
Invoice automation reduces manual entry and matching of vendor invoices.
Which document do you use to bill a customer for something that is not on a sales order?
Free text invoices post directly to ledger accounts without a sales order.
What does a customer posting profile define?
The accounts receivable summary account and related accounts
Customer posting profiles map AR transactions to ledger accounts.
Which workspace or page gives a collector an overview of overdue customer balances and activities?
The Collections page shows aging, transactions, activities and contacts for a customer.
What is an aging snapshot used for?
Grouping customer balances by how long they are overdue
Aging snapshots group balances into aging periods for collections.
Which feature sends reminders to customers with overdue invoices?
Collection letters are reminders based on the overdue status.
Which feature charges customers interest on overdue amounts?
Interest notes calculate and post interest on overdue balances.
What does credit management help with?
Setting credit limits and putting sales orders on hold when limits are exceeded
Credit management uses rules, limits and credit holds.
Which journal do you use to record payments received from customers?
Customer payments are recorded in the customer payment journal.
What is settlement in accounts receivable?
Matching a payment with the invoices it pays
Settlement closes open transactions by matching payments and invoices.
A customer owes a small amount that will never be paid. What do you do?
The write-off function posts the uncollectible amount to a write-off account.
What does a payment schedule do?
Splits an invoice amount into several installments with different due dates
Payment schedules divide the total into installments.
Paying back credit balances to customers
Reimbursement creates vendor transactions to repay customer credit balances.
Checks available budget when documents such as purchase orders are entered
Budget control validates documents and journals against available budget.
Where are basic budget amounts recorded in Finance?
Budget register entries record budget amounts by account and dimension.
Budget codes are used to identify which kinds of budget entries? (Choose two.)
Budget codes classify entries such as original budget, transfer and revision.
Which feature supports a budget process with stages, worksheets and Excel templates?
Budget planning uses processes, stages, workflows and plan documents.
In budget control configuration, what does the budget cycle define?
The time span used to check available budget
The budget cycle (e.g. fiscal year or period) defines over which time budget is checked.
What do fixed asset groups provide?
Default settings for assets, such as books and depreciation
Assets inherit defaults from their fixed asset group.
In fixed assets, what is a book?
A set of values and depreciation rules for an asset, e.g. for tax or accounting
Each asset can have several books, each with its own depreciation.
Which depreciation method spreads the cost evenly over the asset's life?
Straight line gives the same depreciation amount each period.
Which depreciation method calculates depreciation as a percentage of the remaining net book value?
Reducing balance depreciates more at the start and less later.
How can a fixed asset be acquired in Finance? (Choose two.)
Acquisitions can be posted through purchasing or a fixed assets journal.
What are the two disposal types for a fixed asset?
Disposal - sale and disposal - scrap remove the asset from the books.
Which feature calculates the depreciation for many assets each period?
The depreciation proposal creates depreciation lines in the fixed assets journal.
What does a fixed asset posting profile define?
The ledger accounts for asset transactions such as acquisition and depreciation
Fixed asset posting profiles map transaction types to accounts.
You move an asset to another department. Which function do you use?
Transfer moves the asset's values to new financial dimensions or location.
Which transaction increases or decreases an asset's value based on a new valuation?
Write-up and write-down adjustments change the asset's value.
Which tool do you use to design financial statements such as the balance sheet?
Financial reporting uses Report designer with row, column and tree definitions.
In financial reporting, what does the row definition contain?
The lines of the report, such as main accounts and totals
Rows define what appears on each line of the report.
In financial reporting, what does the column definition contain?
Periods and amount types, such as actual vs budget
Columns define the periods and data in each column.
In financial reporting, what is a reporting tree used for?
Showing the report by organization structure, for example per department
Reporting trees define an organizational hierarchy for the report.
Which report lists the balance of every ledger account at a point in time?
The trial balance lists the balance of each account and dimension combination.
What are financial dimension sets used for?
Viewing balances by a chosen combination of dimensions, e.g. in the trial balance
Dimension sets determine how balances are summarized for inquiries and reports.
In Electronic reporting, which component defines the structure of the output file?
The format defines the structure and formatting rules of the file, e.g. XML or Excel.
What should you do before changing a Microsoft-provided ER configuration?
A derived configuration can be rebased when Microsoft releases updates.
Where do you manage ER configurations in Finance?
The Electronic reporting workspace lists configurations and providers.
In Electronic reporting, what does the data model describe?
The business data structure that formats use, independent of the database
The data model is an abstract structure; model mappings fill it from the database.
What is the global address book?
A shared list of parties (people and organizations) used across legal entities
The global address book stores party records and addresses once.
Create unique, readable IDs for records such as vouchers and invoices
Number sequences generate identifiers like voucher numbers.
How can you require approval before a general journal is posted?
Set up a journal approval workflow and enable it on the journal name
Workflows on journal names require approval before posting.
What is cost accounting used for?
Analyzing and allocating costs in a separate cost ledger, without changing the general ledger
Cost accounting collects and allocates costs for management reporting.
What do employees use expense management for?
Creating and submitting expense reports for approval and reimbursement
Employees enter expenses and receipts in expense reports.
What are per diems in expense management?
Per diems pay a set daily amount for meals or lodging while traveling.
Which feature estimates future cash in and out based on open documents?
Cash flow forecasting uses sales, purchases and budgets to forecast cash.
You set a default department on a vendor. What happens?
It defaults on that vendor's transactions
It changes the chart of accounts
Default dimensions on master data are copied to transactions.
How do you usually import opening balances when you go live?
By typing them in a sales order
With data entities in Data management
Data management imports opening balances through data entities.
How can subledger journal entries be transferred to the general ledger?
Synchronously, asynchronously or in a scheduled batch
The transfer can be synchronous, asynchronous or batch-scheduled.
Where do you run long processes in the background, for example a depreciation run?
Batch jobs run processes on the server in the background.
Matches debit and credit transactions on the same ledger account
Ledger settlement marks matching entries, e.g. on clearing accounts, as settled.
Which legal entity setup lets one entity post a transaction for another in the same journal?
Intercompany accounting creates the due to/due from entries automatically.
What are aging period definitions used for?
Defining the time buckets for aged balance reports, e.g. 0-30, 31-60 days
Aging period definitions set the columns of aging reports.
A purchase order invoice is posted. What creates the accounting entries for the expense and AP?
The posting profile and the item/procurement setup
Posting setup determines which accounts are used.
Which feature lets you post a vendor invoice for a service without a purchase order?
Invoice journal (vendor invoice journal) or a non-PO vendor invoice
Vendor invoices without a PO can be entered in an invoice journal or as a non-PO invoice.
Which feature collects related tasks for closing, assigns owners and tracks status across companies?
It manages closing schedules across legal entities.
Which statements about financial dimensions are true? (Choose two.)
They can only be used in sales
They can be custom lists of values
They can be based on existing entities, such as departments
Dimensions can be entity-backed or custom lists; they are used with main accounts, not instead of them.
When you post a customer invoice, where can you see the accounting entries?
In the voucher transactions for the invoice
Voucher transactions show the ledger entries posted for a document.
What happens when you reverse a posted journal entry?
An opposite entry is posted, keeping an audit trail
Reversal creates offsetting entries; posted entries are never deleted.
Which report shows open customer balances by aging bucket?
The customer aged balance report shows overdue amounts by period.
You need the same overhead cost split 60/40 between two departments every month. Which features help? (Choose two.)
Allocation rules split the amount and periodic journals repeat it.
